conversation.content:
Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that this can be a really challenging and overwhelming time for new mothers, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. 

As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a screening tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential concerns related to your emotional well-being during this postpartum period. The purpose of this assessment is to get a better understanding of your emotional state and see if there's anything we can do to support you during this time.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. I want you to feel comfortable and at ease, and I'm here to listen without judgment.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us understand your emotional state over the past 7 days. We'll go through each question together, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and comfortable as possible. 

So, let's get started. The first question is: How have you been feeling about yourself over the past week? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually enjoy, or have you been feeling a bit down or overwhelmed?

.. to be honest, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and tired all the time. I mean, I love my baby, but taking care of her is just so exhausting. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most days, you know? I used to enjoy simple things like reading or watching a movie, but now I just don't have the energy for it. And even when I do try to do something I used to enjoy, it just doesn't feel the same. I feel like I've lost interest in a lot of things that used to bring me happiness.

And to make matters worse, I've been feeling really down and sad a lot of the time. I worry about my baby's health and safety all the time, and it's hard for me to shake off those thoughts. Sometimes I feel like I'm just not doing a good enough job as a mom, and that's a really hard feeling to deal with. I feel guilty and inadequate, like I'm just winging it and hoping for the best. It's hard to explain, but it's just this constant feeling of anxiety and self-doubt that's been really getting to me lately.

I guess what I'm saying is that I just don't feel like myself right now. I feel like I'm just trying to survive each day, rather than actually living and enjoying my life as a new mom. It's hard, because I feel like I should be happy and excited, but the truth is, I'm just really struggling.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

.. I'm not sure I can say that's been true for me lately. I mean, I do laugh sometimes, but it's not like it used to be. I feel like I've lost my sense of humor a bit, and things that used to make me laugh just don't seem as funny anymore. I've been so focused on taking care of the baby and trying to manage my own emotions that I don't really have the energy to find the funny side of things.

Sometimes, when my husband tries to make a joke or lighten the mood, I'll laugh along with him, but it feels kind of forced. I'm just not feeling as carefree and lighthearted as I used to. And to be honest, some days it's hard for me to even muster up a smile. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, and laughter doesn't come as easily as it used to.

I do have moments where I'll be playing with the baby, and she'll do something adorable, and I'll laugh, but it's not like it used to be. It's more of a... I don't know, a tired laugh, I guess. Like, I'm happy in that moment, but it's not a deep, belly laugh like I used to have. Does that make sense.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

.. I don't really feel like I've been looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, I'll have a plan to do something, like go for a walk or meet a friend, and I'll think, "Oh, that sounds nice," but when the time comes, I just don't feel like doing it. I'll feel too tired, or anxious, or just overwhelmed, and I'll end up canceling or putting it off.

And it's not just big things, either. I'll think about doing something small, like taking a shower or reading a book, and I'll feel like, "Ugh, that sounds like too much work." I just don't have the motivation or energy to do things that I used to enjoy. It's like, I know I should be looking forward to these things, but I just don't feel like it.

Sometimes, my husband will suggest we do something, like go out for dinner or see a movie, and I'll think, "That sounds nice," but then I'll start worrying about the baby, and how we'll manage, and whether I'll be able to enjoy myself, and it just feels like too much. So, I'll end up saying no, or putting it off, and just staying home instead.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm missing out on things, and I'm not living the life I want to be living. I just feel so stuck, and overwhelmed, and like I'm just going through the motions. I wish I could look forward to things with enjoyment, like I used to, but it's just not feeling that way right now.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I do that a lot, actually. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If the baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If she's not sleeping well, I think it's because I'm not establishing a good routine. If she's not eating well, I think it's because I'm not making the right food choices. It's like, no matter what happens, I always seem to find a way to blame myself.

And it's not just with the baby, either. I'll be doing something, like cooking dinner or cleaning the house, and if it doesn't turn out right, I'll think, "I'm such a failure. I'm not doing this right." I'll beat myself up over little things, like if I burn a meal or forget to do a load of laundry. It's like, I'm always expecting myself to be perfect, and when I'm not, I feel like I've let everyone down.

I feel like I'm just not good enough, as a mom, as a wife, as a person. I'm always wondering if I'm doing things right, if I'm making the right decisions, if I'm providing enough for my baby. It's exhausting, because I'm always second-guessing myself, and I'm always feeling like I'm falling short.

Sometimes, my husband will try to reassure me, and tell me that I'm doing a great job, but it's hard for me to believe him. I feel like he's just saying that to be nice, and that deep down, he's thinking, "She's not doing this right." It's hard for me to shake off those feelings of self-doubt and blame.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's me all the time, lately. I feel like I'm always worried about something, even when there's no reason to be. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll start thinking, "What if she gets sick? What if she's not gaining enough weight? What if I'm not doing something right?" And it's not just about the baby, either. I'll worry about my husband, and whether he's doing okay, or whether our relationship is suffering because of the baby. I'll worry about our finances, and whether we're going to be able to provide for our family.

It's like, my mind is always racing, and I'm always thinking about all the things that could go wrong. And it's not just rational worries, either. I'll worry about things that are totally irrational, like, "What if the baby stops breathing in her sleep?" or "What if the house catches on fire?" It's like, I know these things are unlikely to happen, but I just can't shake off the feeling of worry and anxiety.

Sometimes, I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll start thinking about all these worst-case scenarios, and I'll get myself so worked up that I'll be lying there, wide awake, feeling like I'm going to have a panic attack. It's hard to calm myself down, and it's hard to shake off those feelings of anxiety and worry.

And the thing is, I know I'm not alone in this. I've talked to other moms, and they've all said that they've experienced similar feelings of anxiety and worry. But it's hard to remember that when you're in the midst of it, you know? It's hard to remember that it's normal, and that it's not just me being crazy or irrational.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times, actually. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, like feeding the baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like, my body is reacting to something, but I don't know what.

Sometimes, it's triggered by something specific, like a loud noise or a sudden movement. But other times, it's just out of the blue. I'll be feeling fine, and then suddenly I'll feel this overwhelming sense of fear and anxiety. It's hard to describe, but it's like my body is on high alert, and I'm waiting for something bad to happen.

When it happens, I try to calm myself down by taking deep breaths and reminding myself that everything is okay. But it's hard to shake off the feeling of panic and fear. Sometimes, I'll get up and walk around the house, or go outside for some fresh air, just to try and clear my head.

It's scary, because I don't know what's causing it, and I don't know how to make it stop. And sometimes, it's hard to explain to my husband or other people what's happening, because it feels so irrational. But at the same time, it feels so real, you know? It's like, my body is telling me that something is wrong, even if my mind knows that everything is okay.

It's happened a few times when I'm alone with the baby, and that's especially scary. I'll be thinking, "What if something happens to me? What if I pass out or something?" And then I'll start worrying about the baby, and how she would be taken care of if something happened to me. It's just this vicious cycle of fear and anxiety, and it's hard to break out of it.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's definitely true for me. I feel like everything is just piling up, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I'm not sleeping much, and when I do, I'm waking up to feed the baby or change her diaper. And even when I'm not directly taking care of her, I'm still thinking about her and worrying about her.

And it's not just the baby, either. I'm also trying to manage the household and take care of my husband and our relationship. I'm trying to cook and clean and do laundry, and it's just feeling like too much. I feel like I'm drowning in a sea of responsibilities, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.

Sometimes, I'll be in the middle of doing something, like making dinner or giving the baby a bath, and I'll just feel overwhelmed. I'll start to feel like I'm going to cry, or like I just can't do it anymore. And it's hard to explain to my husband, because he's trying to be supportive, but he doesn't really understand what I'm going through.

I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, most of the time. And sometimes, I wonder how other moms do it. Like, how do they manage to take care of their babies and their households and themselves, all at the same time? It feels like I'm just barely scraping by, and I'm not doing anything well.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this perfect mom, and I'm just not living up to that. I'm making mistakes, and I'm feeling overwhelmed, and I'm just trying to survive. And it's hard to admit that, because I feel like I'm supposed to be strong and capable, but the truth is, I'm just not feeling that way right now.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been true for me, unfortunately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because of the baby's schedule. I mean, I know that's part of it, but it's more than that. I've just been feeling so unhappy and overwhelmed, and it's hard for me to wind down at night.

I'll lie in bed, and my mind will just start racing. I'll think about all the things I need to do, and all the things I'm worried about, and it's just hard for me to calm down. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll be wide awake for hours. It's like, my brain is just wired to be "on" all the time, and it's hard for me to relax.

And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, it's the quality of sleep, too. I'll sleep for a few hours, but it's not restful sleep. I'll wake up feeling tired and groggy, and it's just hard to start the day when I'm feeling like that.

I've tried to establish a bedtime routine, and I've tried to create a relaxing atmosphere in my bedroom, but it's just not working. I've even tried taking warm baths, and practicing deep breathing, and listening to calming music, but nothing seems to be working.

It's hard, because I know that sleep is so important, especially when you're taking care of a new baby. But it's just not happening for me right now. And it's not just the sleep, it's the overall feeling of unhappiness and overwhelm that's the problem. I just feel like I'm stuck in this rut, and I don't know how to get out of it.

Sometimes, I'll be sitting in the dark, feeding the baby, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. And it's not just about the baby, it's about me, too. I feel like I've lost myself, and I don't know how to get back to being the person I used to be. It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, and I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my new baby, but the truth is, I'm just not feeling that way right now.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been true for me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and it's hard to explain why. I mean, I know I should be happy, I have a beautiful baby, a loving husband, and a comfortable home. But despite all of that, I just can't seem to shake off this feeling of sadness.

It's like, I'll be going about my day, taking care of the baby, doing chores, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. And it's not just a little feeling, it's a big, overwhelming feeling that makes it hard for me to breathe. I'll start to cry, and I won't be able to stop. It's like, my emotions are just so raw and close to the surface, and it's hard for me to keep them under control.

Sometimes, I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just feel this intense love for her, but at the same time, I'll feel this sadness and regret. I'll think about all the things I'm not doing right, all the things I'm not providing for her, and it just makes me feel so miserable.

I've tried to talk to my husband about it, but it's hard for him to understand. He's trying to be supportive, but I can tell he's getting frustrated. He'll say things like, "What's wrong, why are you so sad?" And I'll try to explain, but it's hard to put into words. It's just this feeling of being overwhelmed, and not knowing how to make it better.

I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'm taking care of the baby, I'm doing what I need to do, but I'm not really living. I'm not really experiencing joy, or happiness, or any of the things that I used to feel before the baby was born. It's like, I'm just existing, and it's a really sad, miserable feeling.

Sometimes, I'll have moments where I'll feel okay, where I'll feel like myself again. But they're fleeting, and they're rare. Most of the time, I just feel like I'm stuck in this rut, and I don't know how to get out of it. It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, and I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my new baby. But the truth is, I'm just not feeling that way right now.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been crying a lot, and it's not just a little bit of crying, either. I'm talking about full-on, sobbing, can't-catch-my-breath crying. It's like, my emotions are just so raw and close to the surface, and it's hard for me to keep them under control.

I'll be doing something normal, like feeding the baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's like, my body is just releasing all of this pent-up emotion, and I'm powerless to stop it. I've cried in front of my husband, I've cried in front of my family, I've even cried in front of strangers. It's just so embarrassing, but at the same time, it's like my body is just trying to release all of this stress and anxiety that I've been carrying around.

Sometimes, I'll cry because I'm feeling overwhelmed, and I just don't know how to keep going. Sometimes, I'll cry because I'm feeling guilty, and I'm worried that I'm not doing a good enough job as a mom. And sometimes, I'll cry just because I'm feeling so sad, and I don't know how to make it better.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be strong, and I'm supposed to be able to handle all of this. But the truth is, I'm just not feeling that way right now. I'm feeling weak, and I'm feeling vulnerable, and I'm feeling like I'm just barely holding it together.

I've tried to talk to my husband about it, and he's trying to be supportive, but it's hard for him to understand. He'll say things like, "It's okay, you're just stressed," or "You're just tired," but it's more than that. It's like, my whole world has been turned upside down, and I'm just trying to find my footing again.

I guess what I'm saying is, I'm just feeling really overwhelmed, and I'm not sure how to make it better. I'm hoping that by talking to you, I can start to figure some things out, and I can start to feel like myself again. Because right now, I just feel like I'm lost, and I'm not sure how to find my way back.
